name: Amoud Foundation
mission: Founded in 1998, the Amoud Foundation impacts the local and global communities by helping people help themselves through sustainable humanitarian projects while maintaining trusting relationships. Amoud is an international humanitarian organization that today serves the people in the Horn of Africa. Amoud also does work on the home-front including helping with the 2006 Hurricane Relief and 2015 Garland Tornado recovery.

strengths_deep_dive: Amoud Foundation exhibits high financial allocation toward direct service delivery. In FY2024, <cite id="1">89.3% of funds went to program expenses</cite>, beating the peer program ratio median of 83.3%. Fundraising operations remain lean, requiring just <cite id="1"><$0.01 per $1 raised</cite>. Furthermore, its <cite id="1">12.7 months of working capital</cite> provides a stable base to protect basic services like orphan centers and schools during emergency shifts.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1998, Amoud Foundation provides humanitarian assistance, education, and healthcare across East Africa. The organization focuses its operations primarily on supporting 15 orphan centers and two schools for the deaf and blind in Somaliland and Somalia <cite id="2">through targeted community programs</cite>. In FY2024, the foundation managed <cite id="5">$11,142,566 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting steady growth from prior operational years. Financial metrics indicate strong operational discipline, with a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 92.4% in FY2024</cite> and fundraising costs remaining under <$0.01 per $1 raised. Amoud Foundation operates explicit zakat-eligible relief initiatives <cite id="2">serving verified categories of need</cite>. While direct service delivery is high, independent governance structures and clear cost-per-beneficiary outcome metrics remain limited.
